name: MetaClaw
vibe_summary: An OpenClaw-adjacent agent layer that meta-learns and evolves skills from every conversation, no GPU cluster required. It pairs a persistent cross-session memory layer with scheduled RL training (via Tinker) for a self-improving personal agent.
best_for: Users who want an agent that improves from conversation history
Experimenters interested in RL fine-tuning without GPU clusters
OpenClaw users wanting persistent cross-session memory
avoid_if: You need a battle-tested, large-community project
You want zero external training-service dependencies (RL mode needs Tinker)
You require hardened sandboxing for untrusted shell execution
openclaw_advantages: Built-in skill evolution and RL training loop
Cross-session memory with automatic fact injection
Incremental memory ingestion reduces mid-session blackout
One-click setup wizard and async architecture
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community and ecosystem than OpenClaw
RL mode depends on external Tinker service
Younger codebase with less security hardening
Reddit/web footprint is thin and mostly indirect
confidence_summary: Strong evidence from README, releases, and detailed commit history for architecture and activity claims. Community sentiment is weakly evidenced — Reddit matches are mostly unrelated keyword collisions, so sentiment and adoption scores carry real uncertainty.

overview_markdown:
MetaClaw is a Python-based agent framework that positions itself as a self-improving layer on top of the OpenClaw ecosystem: you talk to your agent, and it meta-learns and evolves skills from every conversation. Its headline architecture combines three modes — a Skills mode (no external dependencies), an RL mode that fine-tunes via the Tinker training service without requiring a local GPU cluster, and a default Auto mode that runs skills plus scheduled RL training. Setup is deliberately minimal: `metaclaw setup` then `metaclaw start`.

The v0.4.x line introduced the Contexture memory layer, which persists cross-session user and project memory and automatically injects relevant facts into prompts. The v0.4.1 release added incremental memory ingestion — turns are extracted and persisted every N turns (default 5) instead of only at session end — exposed through sidecar endpoints (`/buffer_turn`, `/flush_session`) and an OpenClaw plugin (`openclaw-metaclaw-memory`) written in TypeScript. Recent commits show active maintenance: Windows cross-platform fixes (pid detection, PATHEXT resolution, path-with-spaces handling), a configurable `max_context_tokens`, and a benchmark suite (metaclaw-bench) with per-day workspace fixtures.

Compared to OpenClaw proper, MetaClaw is less a full assistant and more a learning/memory substrate that plugs into OpenClaw-style agents. Its differentiator is the evolution loop — skill extraction plus RL fine-tuning from real usage — rather than channel breadth or UI polish. The trade-offs are a much smaller community, a dependency on an external training service for RL mode, and a younger, less security-hardened codebase.
